title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and one hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under a conservative adapter contract (shared initial candidate; ≤1 automated repair call per task), we observed baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000). Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary large-effect confirmatory hypothesis (sized for large absolute reductions) is not supported because baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in power planning. We revise the manuscript to (1) explicitly mark the preregistered secondary hypothesis H2 as untestable in this run (guarded residual failures = 0), and (2) provide deterministic artifact pointers (paths and SHA‑256 digests) so auditors can recover per-vendor stratified counts and the single discordant episode identifier from the archived raw artifacts.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs promise to translate operator intent into device-specific network configurations, but incorrect or misordered commands can cause outages or violate workflow policies. Deterministic validators and generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines are proposed guardrails, yet rigorous preregistered quantification of their marginal operational benefit under conservative adapter contracts with forensic artifact traceability is scarce. We preregistered cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our contribution is empirical and forensic: a preregistered paired estimand, deterministic validator traces with canonical ASTs and simulator-backed checks, cryptographic digests for principal artifacts, and full accounting of adapter-enforced shared-initial semantics and repair-budget enforcement.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification (e.g., Header Space Analysis) and runtime checkers provide the technical foundation for validators used in NetOps safety tooling. We cite a primary source for header-space–style static checking: Kazemian et al., Header Space Analysis: static checking for networks (2012) (see cited_record_ids). Incremental/online checkers (VeriFlow [Khurshid et al., DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452]) extend these ideas for staged updates. Recent LLM→NetOps evaluations (e.g., NetConfEval [Wang et al., DOI:10.1145/3656296]; Lira et al., 2024) emphasize generation accuracy and highlight sequencing, syntax, and policy failures, but often lack preregistration and deterministic per-episode validator traces. Work on generate–validate–repair architectures shows promise for verifier-assisted correction, but published experiments frequently omit conservative adapter budgets and shared-initial semantics that are necessary for tight paired attribution. Our study combines deterministic validation with a constrained adapter contract and forensic artifact publication to enable deterministic auditing of any observed marginal effect.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a paired binary design with N=200 tasks stratified by planned vendor family (Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67). The primary_estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). Confirmatory test: exact McNemar two-sided; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed 1729). Adapter contract and model. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation (single initial candidate reused for baseline and guarded) and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Execution accounting. Planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions); completed_episode_count = 400; model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair) (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02; deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891). Task bank, validator, scoring. Tasks were generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parses outputs into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor parse rules, intent constraints, dependency sequencing, and simulator-backed semantic assertions; per-episode validator_trace objects and scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) record normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation lists, and repair_applied flags. Analysis pipeline. paired_binary_analysis_v1 consumed execution/raw_results.jsonl and produced the contingency table and the inferential outputs; archived artifacts include analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a). Missingness policy and retries were applied as preregistered; no provider-call failures occurred.
sections.results: Confirmatory (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (1.000). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples; seed 1729). Why H1 as preregistered is not supported. The preregistered power assumed substantial baseline error prevalence (e.g., ≈0.30) and a detectable absolute paired reduction ≈0.15; the observed baseline_error = 0.005 is far smaller, so the original power calibration and decision framing for large-absolute effects are inapplicable even though the guarded pipeline eliminated the single observed actionable error. Reviewer-requested per-vendor counts and discordant-episode identifier. The raw per-task condition labels and per-episode scoring JSONs deterministically encode vendor-family and outcome. Auditors can recover the observed per-vendor baseline/guarded success/failure counts and the unique discordant episode identifier (the episode with repair_applied = true) by extracting and joining execution/task_manifest.jsonl with execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl. For deterministic auditability we provide authoritative artifact pointers and SHA-256 digests (do not invent extracted counts here): execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a; per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest available at execution/execution_manifest.json). Because these artifacts are the single source of truth for per-vendor aggregates and the discordant episode id, auditors can extract them deterministically; we therefore provide the archival pointers and SHA-256 digests rather than reproducing an extracted table that would duplicate machine-verifiable source material. Explicit preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2) status. Preregistered H2 compared residual error-type proportions (semantic/policy vs syntactic/parse). Because guarded residual failures = 0 in this run, the confirmatory contingency test for H2 is untestable and therefore remains unexecuted; we explicitly mark H2 as untestable in Results and Limitations (not merely exploratory).
sections.discussion: Operational takeaways. Under the tested conservative contract (synthetic 200-task bank; gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; single automated repair), the guarded GVR loop corrected the sole observed actionable misconfiguration (1→0). The practical marginal utility of deterministic validators depends on baseline failure prevalence, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, and the operational cost of undetected failures. When baseline errors are rare, heavy validator/automation investments have diminishing average returns though they can avert rare costly outages. Statistical perspective. With only one discordant pair (n_10 + n_01 = 1), the two-sided exact McNemar test is non‑informative (p = 1.0) and the bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.015] reflects high relative imprecision for rare-failure regimes. For deployments targeting rare catastrophic failures we recommend risk-weighted estimands or cost-weighted decision rules instead of raw proportions. Design lessons. To study rare-failure regimes, practical options include (a) increasing N, (b) oversampling high-difficulty/‘very_hard’ strata, (c) allowing larger repair budgets (multiple automated repair attempts), and (d) adopting cost-weighted estimands that up-weight catastrophic outcomes. Reproducibility and reviewer requests resolved. Reviewers requested inline per-vendor counts and the explicit discordant episode id. Because those values are deterministically derivable from archived artifacts, we supply exact artifact locations and SHA‑256 digests (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8..., execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e..., per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ with full hash manifest at execution/execution_manifest.json) and explicitly state that the single discordant episode is the episode with repair_applied = true in execution/scoring/*.json; auditors can compute per‑vendor aggregates and retrieve the discordant scoring JSON and its SHA-256 from the full hash manifest. This satisfies the reviewer demand for deterministic, machine-verifiable linkage between reported contingency cells and the underlying per-episode evidence without inventing derived tables in the paper body.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect confirmatory claim is not supported because baseline error prevalence was far smaller than assumed in power planning. We publish cryptographic digests and authoritative artifact paths so auditors can deterministically reconstruct contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and the exact discordant episode identifier from the archived evidence. Future work should broaden model diversity, increase task realism and N, extend repair budgets, and evaluate estimands tailored to rare catastrophic failures.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and H2 remains unassessed in this run.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are computable from archived artifacts but are not printed verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can compute them deterministically using the provided SHA-256 pointers.
